newsitem.title: USA: Chevron raises capital spending to $5.9 bln.
newsitem.headline: Chevron raises capital spending to $5.9 bln.

text.p: Chevron Corp plans capital spending in 1997 to total about $5.9 billion, up from $4.9 billion in 1996, Chairman Kenneth Derr said at the annual meeting here.
Derr said the company's budget for downstream refining, marketing and transportation operations would increase about 15 percent in 1997 to $1.4 billion.
Also speaking at the meeting, Vice Chairman James Sullivan said some of the upstream budget would go to drilling 15 new wells in the U.S. Gulf over the next four years.
The wells are planned for the U.S. Gulf's Norphlet field.

"Only recently have technology and experience brought promising prospects in the Gulf's deep water within reach," Sullivan told shareholders. He cited Genesis -- a $750-million project that will produce oil and natural gas from a "floating spar structure" -- as the company's premier deep-water Gulf of Mexico endeavor.

Chevron currently has exploration and production activities in 21 countries. Derr identified the Tengiz field in Kazakhstan and a significant discovery offshore Angola as some of the company's most promising upstream projects overseas.
